D66·7psk — 2026-10-19
chose: 8.5: a task-policy run nudges a session whose context passes the session ceiling: --session-ceiling <tokens>, default the repo's context ceiling (context-ceiling settings, 200k tokens) when that ceiling is given in tokens, `off` for none. A per-driver knob, not recorded, like --max-stalls. The nudge carries kind "ceiling", and both hook implementations (TS nudgeLine, Rust nudge_line) turn it into: commit what you have, write back with this task still active and its exact next step, end the turn. A session nudged this way that wrote back is a `threshold` handoff even with no task resolved: no stall, and the next session takes the task fresh. A task's 4th ceiling handoff in one run counts as a stall, so a task that cannot fit under the ceiling still stops the run through --max-stalls.
over: a cumulative-token cap (the adapter reports only the latest turn's context plus output; per-turn cost scales with context, so context is the lever); killing the session at the cap (loses uncommitted work and the write-back); a new handoff reason (schema change; `threshold` already means "the gauge moved"); applying it to the threshold policy, which already has --threshold-pct
because: felt-latency sessions reached 25.8M tokens per task by re-reading a context that kept growing. A fresh session resuming from the write-back pays a small prompt instead. The repo's ceiling is already the operator's stated limit for interactive sessions, so a driven session obeys the same number. The per-task cap keeps the no-stall handoff from looping forever.
